messages:
alex_support: FYI ACME (acct: acme-corp) is seeing streaming responses drop with a broken pipe around 30-50s. They say we counted it as a 5xx and billed. request_id=rid-9f1c. Repro attached below.

incident-bot: automatic alert: proxy-5xx-spike detected for rid-9f1c (sample size: 7 failures, window: 5m) :bangbang:

ingrid_sre: can you paste the client curl + proxy/runtime logs for rid-9f1c? also which SDK/version?

alex_support: curl we used to repro:
```
curl -v -N -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \"https://api.redwood.ai/v1/chat?stream=true\" \n  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \n  -d '{"messages":[{"role":"user","content":"hi"}], "max_tokens":1024}'
```
client shows: "write failed: broken pipe" after ~42s.

proxy log (trimmed):
```
[proxy] 2026-03-12T21:13:02.421Z rid=rid-9f1c method=POST path=/v1/chat?stream=true vhost=api redir=none upstream=10.2.5.12:8080 status=502 proto=http/1.1 msg="upstream write error: write: broken pipe"
[proxy] 2026-03-12T21:13:02.421Z rid=rid-9f1c resp_bytes=0
```

runtime log (same request):
```
[runtime] 2026-03-12T21:13:02.420Z rid=rid-9f1c stream_state=generating token_idx=184 kvcache_hit=false
[runtime] 2026-03-12T21:13:02.421Z rid=rid-9f1c write_error: broken pipe (syscall: write)
```

headers show: `Transfer-Encoding: chunked`, client is a custom agent (node SDK v2.5).

leo_runtime: likely scenario: client TCP FIN/close arrived while runtime was mid-stream. proxy observed write->broken pipe and mapped to upstream failure -> returned 502/5xx and our billing pipeline flagged it. We need to distinguish client-initiated disconnects from runtime errors. Right now ECONNRESET/write: broken pipe gets classified as upstream 5xx.

leo_runtime: quick repro idea: run tcpdump on client machine and server side to confirm FIN arrival time vs last server write. Also try reproducing with a small keepalive ping (send a single extra newline every 10s) to see if it prevents client-side close.

ingrid_sre: +1 on tcpdump. Can someone attach pcap or show connection traces? Also which LB/proxy layer recorded the 502? We need the proxy->billing tag pipeline correlation (log id).

alex_support: attached pcap snippet (uploaded to ticket). customer says they did not intentionally close; they use an HTTP proxy in their infra which may drop idle conns after 30s. They saw idle gaps between chunks ~14-18s sometimes.

maya_prodeng: blocking item: until runtime/proxy change, we should avoid charging customers for these. Action: create rule to not bill requests where proxy log shows upstream write error AND we have evidence of client FIN within +/-100ms of the write error. cc @ingrid_sre @leo_runtime.

leo_runtime: agreed. I'll add a short-term filter in the billing classifier: if proxy_log contains "upstream write error" and tcp_trace indicates client FIN (SYN/FIN flags) immediately prior, mark as client-abort (no-bill). I'll open PR and a canary.

ingrid_sre: long-term: improve heuristic to inspect TCP half-close vs runtime exception. Also instrument a small header we can emit when client-initiated close is detected (e.g., X-Client-Disconnect) so downstream can avoid 5xx tagging.

alex_support: customer asks for ETA and credits. can we offer immediate credit while this is investigated? :eyes:

maya_prodeng: yes, offer a one-time credit for the billed requests and say we're investigating. I'll prepare the CC note.

leo_runtime: next steps:
- repro with tcpdump + node sdk disable proxy keepalive (today)
- patch billing classifier to ignore these patterns (WIP, today/tonight)
- instrument X-Client-Disconnect header (short RFC, next week)
- post-mortem + runbook update (ingrid)

ingrid_sre: assigning to eng-runtime oncall (leo) to start the tracer capture. I'll keep the slack thread for updates. :thumbsup:

alex_support: noted, keeping customer updated. thanks all.
